findings.statement: Open Targets association with ccRCC is moderate, driven by literature rather than genetics [gene=CA9; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.3088]. Tractable as antibody (AB: Advanced Clinical), small molecule (SM: Approved Drug) and PROTAC binder. Drugs as returned: GIRENTUXIMAB PHASE_3, IODINE I 124 GIRENTUXIMAB PHASE_2, SULTHIAME PHASE_4, ETHOXZOLAMIDE WITHDRAWAL. UniProt: cell membrane and microvillus membrane, so it is accessible to antibodies and suitable as an imaging or biomarker target. Reactome: HIF-regulated gene expression. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependence and no selectivity and it is not common-essential, so this is an antibody-targeting or imaging target (an expression-restricted marker) and not a functional dependency. It is essentially never mutated (not recurrent). PRISM best compound (para-toluenesulfonamide) has several annotated targets and is not significant, so it is uninformative.

Strongly tumour-up in TCGA, with a low Open Targets association score and a mid-table rank, so prior association is weak. Tractable by antibody and cell therapy (AB: Advanced Clinical, OC: Advanced Clinical). Drugs as returned: CUSATUZUMAB PHASE_2, VORSETUZUMAB PHASE_1, VORSETUZUMAB MAFODOTIN PHASE_1, MDX-1411 PHASE_1. UniProt: plasma membrane ligand of CD27 (immune checkpoint-like axis). DepMap: no ccRCC dependence, not common-essential, so CD70 is a surface-antigen target for ADC, antibody or CAR-T and not a cell-intrinsic dependency. Not recurrently mutated in the returned data.

Tumour-up and purity-robust in the convergence ranking, with a low Open Targets score. Tractable by antibody-drug conjugate or oncology-class modality (OC: Advanced Clinical) and small molecule (high-quality ligand). Drug as returned: AGS-16C3F PHASE_2. UniProt: apical cell membrane and secreted, so it is accessible and potentially measurable as a soluble biomarker. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency and it is not common-essential. This is an untested-in-label but clinically explored surface target, and its case rests on expression restriction and not on dependency.

Ranked first in the convergence target profile, with replicated tumour upregulation (RNA and protein) and a genetic-association component in Open Targets. Tractability is antibody-accessible and small-molecule (druggable family, high-quality ligand), but OpenTargets returns no approved or clinical drug. UniProt: cell membrane and caveola. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency and no selectivity (not common-essential), so there is druggability without demonstrated dependency, which is a weaker target case. A plausible biomarker or lipid-uptake mechanism gene to validate.

Rank 3 in the convergence ranking. Tumour-up (RNA and protein) with some literature support. Tractability: antibody-accessible and small-molecule ligand, but no approved or clinical drug is returned. Pathways: proton-coupled monocarboxylate transport and basigin interactions (lactate efflux, glycolytic phenotype). DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency (not selective, not common-essential), so inhibition is not supported as a single-agent strategy in 2D lines. The mechanism is metabolic and untested clinically.

Strong biomarker profile: tumour-up and the only top candidate with TCGA survival evidence in this set (higher expression linked to worse outcome in the ranking record). Tractability is small-molecule only (druggable family, high-quality ligand, structure with ligand), with no drug returned. Pathways: nicotinate metabolism and methylation. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency and the sign is slightly opposite to selectivity, so it is better framed as a prognostic or metabolic biomarker than a target.

Tumour-up lipid-metabolism gene. Roughly two fifths of ccRCC lines are dependent but selectivity versus other lines is negative, so dependency is not ccRCC-specific (not common-essential). The PRISM compound plurisin-#1 (stearoyl-CoA desaturase inhibitor, single annotated target, preclinical) shows no ccRCC selectivity. Treat as a mechanism or context-dependent candidate and not as a selective target.

Established ccRCC drug target (HIF-2 alpha). Drug as returned: BELZUTIFAN APPROVAL. Tractable by small molecule (approved drug). Open Targets association is in the top ten for ccRCC. Reactome: HIF regulation, hypoxia response and PD-L1 transcription. DepMap shows the clearest selective dependency among the reviewed genes in ccRCC lines versus others [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.3] and it is not common-essential, although the multiple-testing-adjusted p is borderline. A minority of ccRCC lines are dependent, consistent with 2D culture only partly capturing HIF-2 biology.

Established ccRCC drug target (VEGFR2), with a large drug set at all stages. Approved agents as returned include AXITINIB, PAZOPANIB HYDROCHLORIDE, TIVOZANIB HYDROCHLORIDE, CABOZANTINIB S-MALATE, LENVATINIB MESYLATE, SORAFENIB TOSYLATE and RAMUCIRUMAB (all APPROVAL), plus SUNITINIB (PHASE_4). Antibody and small molecule tractability are both labelled approved. The target is endothelial, so tumour-cell DepMap shows no dependency (not selective, not common-essential), which is expected and reflects a microenvironment mechanism and not tumour-cell addiction. Reactome: VEGFA-VEGFR2 pathway.

Established ccRCC drug target. Drug as returned: RIDAFOROLIMUS APPROVAL, together with a long list of PI3K/mTOR kinase inhibitors at early to late clinical phases. Recurrently mutated in ccRCC at a frequency of [gene=MTOR; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.072]. It is a common-essential gene, with a strongly negative effect in ccRCC lines [gene=MTOR; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; mean_effect_ccrcc=-1.52] and only modest selectivity, so there is a therapeutic-window and toxicity risk. PRISM best compound WAY-600 (mTOR inhibitor, single target, preclinical) is not significant after correction.

Association-only driver gene: second-highest Open Targets association with ccRCC. The most frequently mutated gene reviewed here [gene=PBRM1; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.362]. It is a tumour suppressor lost in disease, so the DepMap effect is not negative in ccRCC lines (no dependency, not common-essential). It is not directly druggable and is relevant for stratification or synthetic-lethality hypotheses only.

caveats: Several top-ranked genes (SCARB1, SLC16A3, NNMT, CA9, CD70, ENPP3) show no ccRCC DepMap dependency, so their case is expression-restricted antigen or biomarker use and not functional dependency.
DepMap and PRISM use 2D cell lines and miss HIF-2 and microenvironment biology (KDR is endothelial).
Open Targets association scores are low for many novel candidates, reflecting limited prior literature and not absence of relevance.
Drug stages are reported as returned by Open Targets and may include non-ccRCC indications; the mention of an approved drug does not mean approval in ccRCC.
I did not call STRING interactions and reviewed only the top part of the convergence ranking and a subset of the top disease genes (VHL, SETD2, BAP1, KDM5C not individually profiled).
The CA9 PRISM compound has several annotated targets and is uninformative for a single gene.
